title.purpose: Page titles, section headings, dialog headings. Tight leading for density.

body.purpose: Primary content, descriptions, prose. Cap at 65–75ch in reading contexts.

label.purpose: Navigation items, button labels, form labels, table headers. The majority of visible text.

caption.purpose: Timestamps, meta text, secondary identifiers, status strings.

mono.purpose: API keys, integration IDs, code references, technical values. Visual signal that a value is literal and copyable.

shadows.name: panel-dark
shadows.purpose: Floating containers in dark theme: dropdowns, modals, tooltips.

shadows.name: chrome
shadows.purpose: Sidebar and navbar — accent-tinted structural chrome. Creates warmth; distinguishes chrome from content.

shadows.name: avatar-glow
shadows.purpose: Tight ambient glow on accent-tinted avatar and identity badges.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Deep modal dialog shadow. Heavier than standard panel shadow to communicate elevation and focus.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions. Exits fast, enters slow — feels responsive.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Interactive feedback: hover states, focus rings, button color shifts.

narrative.overview:
Cortex's visual system is designed to disappear. It is not a UI that announces itself; it is a surface that earns trust by staying out of the way while keeping everything present. The dominant mode is dark, not as an aesthetic choice but a functional one: enterprise operations teams working across multiple systems in long sessions need an environment that doesn't fatigue the eye or fragment attention. The Indigo Depth backgrounds create dimensional space without darkness for its own sake. Signal Teal activates selectively — a current flowing through the system to mark what matters.

The aesthetic philosophy is calibrated density. There is no whitespace inflation. Surfaces layer tonally through the background → surface → surface-secondary → surface-tertiary progression, each step a quiet signal that something has elevated, without a shadow announcing it. When shadows do appear, they carry an accent tint: the system's warmth surfacing at points of structure. The floating sidebar and navbar — rounded, bounded, gently shadowed — make the chrome feel like it belongs inside the space rather than framing it from the outside.

This system explicitly rejects two failure modes: generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics (white cards on white backgrounds, identical icon-heading-text grids, hero-metric templates) and AI hype aesthetics (purple-to-blue gradients, neural network backgrounds, 'powered by AI' badges). Cortex demonstrates intelligence through behavior, not through labeling.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first with tonal depth through surface layering, not shadows at rest
One accent, rarely used, always meaningful
Floating, rounded chrome (sidebar and navbar) that sits inside the viewport
Single system font family — legibility over personality
Accent-tinted shadows on primary structural surfaces

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal appears on ≤10% of any screen at a time. Accent backgrounds use color-mix at 12–16% opacity. Accent borders use 22–48% opacity. Full-saturation accent is reserved for focus rings and active state icons. Its scarcity is structural, not accidental.

rules.name: The Tonal Progression Rule
rules.body: Surfaces step up in both lightness and chroma together: background (0.145/0.018) → surface (0.185/0.020) → surface-secondary (0.225/0.022) → surface-tertiary (0.265/0.024). Breaking it — skipping a level, reversing direction — signals an error, not a design decision.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: All primary chrome surfaces use color-mix blending Signal Teal 30–35% with black as their shadow color. Pure black shadows are reserved for floating panels only. The accent's warmth follows the structure.

rules.name: The No-Display Rule
rules.body: No editorial, serif, or variable font appears in this product. Every element uses the same system sans. Size and weight carry hierarchy; the typeface does not.

rules.name: The Three-Weight Rule
rules.body: Three weights only: 400 (body, captions), 500 (labels, buttons, active navigation), 600 (headings, titles). Weight contrast of at least 100 between adjacent hierarchy levels.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows appear only as a response to state or structural role. A surface at rest is flat. A surface that floats has a shadow. No decorative box-shadows on content cards or list items at rest.

dos: Do use the tonal surface system for elevation: background → surface → surface-secondary → surface-tertiary in that order.
Do reserve Signal Teal for state: active selection, focus rings, current nav item, success indicators.
Do use color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent) 12–24%, transparent) for tinted backgrounds and inner borders.
Do float the sidebar and navbar: my-3 ml-3, rounded-2xl, border border-border, warm chrome shadow.
Do use rounded-xl (12px) for panels; rounded-2xl (16px) for chrome; rounded-md (6px) for interactive controls.
Do use skeleton states (animate-pulse bg-surface-secondary) for loading content. Never a centered spinner.
Do ensure both dark and light themes meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for all text and interactive elements.
Do add accent-tinted shadows on structural chrome surfaces.
donts: Don't build identical card grids: icon + heading + text, repeated at identical sizes.
Don't use the hero-metric template: big number, small label, gradient accent, supporting stats.
Don't use purple-to-blue gradients, neural network backgrounds, glowing orbs, particle animations, or 'powered by AI' badges.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, list items, alerts, or callouts.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient fill (gradient text).
Don't use modal dialogs as a first thought for secondary actions.
Don't use decorative motion — entrance choreography, scroll-driven sequences, bounce or elastic easings.
Don't use Signal Teal as a large background fill. It is a signal, not a surface.
Don't apply display fonts, serif typefaces, or editorial font pairings to UI labels, buttons, or navigation.
Don't nest cards. A container inside a container becomes a section — never a card inside a card.
